questions.prompt: Why is Angular best described as a framework rather than a programming language?
options: It supplies application conventions and APIs while application code uses TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
It is a replacement for HTML and CSS.
It is a database engine.
It is a programming language that replaces TypeScript.
questions.answer_key: It supplies application conventions and APIs while application code uses TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
questions.explanation: Angular is a framework; TypeScript and the browser runtime have distinct roles.

questions.prompt: Which Angular template block should be the primary modern choice for conditionally displaying content?
options: A route guard.
@if
*ngIf is required for every new template.
A direct document.write call.
questions.answer_key: @if
questions.explanation: The curriculum emphasizes modern built-in @if/@else syntax while keeping structural directives for legacy projects.

questions.prompt: What is the key reason to include track in a modern @for block?
options: To load arbitrary modules from user data.
To replace list data with CSS.
To associate rendered rows with stable identities and reduce unnecessary DOM work.
To authorize each record on the server.
questions.answer_key: To associate rendered rows with stable identities and reduce unnecessary DOM work.
questions.explanation: Tracking by stable identity helps Angular reuse existing DOM nodes when collections change.

questions.prompt: What do Angular signals primarily provide?
options: Automatic authorization of API calls.
A replacement for all asynchronous APIs.
A database transaction layer.
Reactive value reads and dependency tracking for state changes.
questions.answer_key: Reactive value reads and dependency tracking for state changes.
questions.explanation: Signals notify consumers when their values change and help Angular track dependencies.

questions.prompt: Which layer must enforce authorization for protected business operations?
options: The trusted backend/API.
Only a component template.
A CSS class.
A client-side route guard alone.
questions.answer_key: The trusted backend/API.
questions.explanation: UI checks improve the experience but do not enforce access to trusted resources.

questions.prompt: What does a successful TypeScript type check prove?
options: That the app is accessible.
That the checked code satisfies the selected type rules, not that untrusted data is valid at runtime.
That every API response is safe.
That no browser runtime errors can occur.
questions.answer_key: That the checked code satisfies the selected type rules, not that untrusted data is valid at runtime.
questions.explanation: Static type checks help catch contract errors; runtime validation and tests still matter.

questions.prompt: What is a good form validation design?
options: Trust browser validation for all business rules.
Disable keyboard access to prevent errors.
Use clear constraints, field-level feedback, accessible associations and server validation for submitted data.
Display errors only by changing field colors.
questions.answer_key: Use clear constraints, field-level feedback, accessible associations and server validation for submitted data.
questions.explanation: Validation should be understandable and accessible; the backend validates authoritative rules.

questions.prompt: Why do Angular services use dependency injection?
options: To embed secrets in frontend code.
To prevent unit testing.
To convert TypeScript into SQL.
To make dependencies explicit and configurable within provider scopes.
questions.answer_key: To make dependencies explicit and configurable within provider scopes.
questions.explanation: Dependency injection supports reuse, testability and managed service lifetimes.

questions.prompt: How should an HTTP feature represent a failed request?
options: With an explicit error state and a recovery path appropriate to the operation.
As a successful empty result in every case.
By silently ignoring errors.
By showing a permanent spinner.
questions.answer_key: With an explicit error state and a recovery path appropriate to the operation.
questions.explanation: Loading, empty, success and failure are different states.

questions.prompt: What is hydration in an Angular SSR app?
options: Generating component CSS at compile time.
Reusing server-rendered DOM while the client application starts.
Encrypting every response.
Creating a database schema.
questions.answer_key: Reusing server-rendered DOM while the client application starts.
questions.explanation: Hydration lets Angular attach client behavior to rendered markup and can avoid unnecessary DOM recreation.

questions.prompt: Which rendering mode is usually appropriate for pages that can be produced at build time and rarely need request-specific data?
options: A live WebSocket subscription for every request.
A form control.
Prerendering/static generation.
Client-side routing guard.
questions.answer_key: Prerendering/static generation.
questions.explanation: Prerendering can deliver generated HTML from static hosting for suitable routes.

questions.prompt: What should a performance investigation begin with?
options: A broad rewrite without a baseline.
Increasing bundle size preemptively.
Removing all tests.
A reproducible measurement or profile of the observed bottleneck.
questions.answer_key: A reproducible measurement or profile of the observed bottleneck.
questions.explanation: Measure actual behavior first and compare after a targeted change.

questions.prompt: Which animation approach is the modern focus in this curriculum?
options: animate.enter / animate.leave with CSS, after checking the target Angular version.
Legacy triggers for all new projects without review.
Direct innerHTML replacement.
Using motion that cannot be disabled.
questions.answer_key: animate.enter / animate.leave with CSS, after checking the target Angular version.
questions.explanation: The official documentation presents enter/leave APIs and CSS; legacy animations remain migration material.

questions.topic: Attribute and Structural Directives in Component APIs
questions.prompt: What is required for a safe Angular migration?
options: Remove all lockfiles and skip the build.
A compatibility plan, stepwise update, tests and a recovery path.
Change major dependencies blindly on production.
Ignore deprecation warnings.
questions.answer_key: A compatibility plan, stepwise update, tests and a recovery path.
questions.explanation: Angular upgrades should follow supported version paths and be verified with tests.

questions.prompt: What should a release checklist include?
options: Production credentials in frontend code.
A claim that deployment succeeded before running it.
Dependency and security review, tests, versioned environment configuration, build evidence and rollback readiness.
Only a screenshot of the home page.
questions.answer_key: Dependency and security review, tests, versioned environment configuration, build evidence and rollback readiness.
questions.explanation: A release decision should rely on actual verifiable evidence, not assumptions.
